song_story.overview: BBoom BBoom (뿜뿜) is MOMOLAND's 2018 breakout hit, and the whole song is built to be maximally addictive and imitable — a simple 'finger heart gun' dance and a chorus made almost entirely of one repeated sound effect. Underneath the silliness, the lyrics are about being completely thrown off balance by someone you're falling for: your heart racing, your composure gone, your knees literally going weak, all condensed into the onomatopoeia 뿜뿜 (bboom bboom), which mimics a heart pounding or fluttering out of control.
song_story.cultural_root: The song leans entirely on onomatopoeia as emotional shorthand, a technique Korean pop uses constantly — 두근두근 (heart pounding), 뿜뿜 (an exaggerated pop/burst sound here standing for infatuation), 콱 막히다 (to feel suddenly choked up). Rather than describing the feeling of a crush in sentences, the song just performs the physical sensations as sound, which is part of why the hook translates so easily across language barriers — you don't need to know Korean to feel what 뿜뿜 is doing.

verse_1.literal: My heart flutters, at our rendezvous, you and me / you pick my heart up and put it down however you please
verse_1.context: 들었다 놨다 하다 — 'to pick up and put down [repeatedly]' — is an idiom for someone toying with your emotions, making you feel elated then uncertain, over and over. 맘대루 is a casual pronunciation of 맘대로 (as one pleases), emphasizing she has no control over how he affects her.

verse_2.lines: 너를 들었다 놓을 거야neoreul deureotda noeul geoya / 넌 점점 더 fall in loveneon jeomjeom deo fall in love / My 눈눈눈눈눈눈 눈빛My nunnunnunnunnunnun nunbit / 쏟아지는ssodajineun / My 터터터터터터 터치My teoteoteoteoteoteo teochi / 하나뿐인hanappunin / 내 머리부터 뿜뿜nae meoributeo ppumppum / 내 발끝까지 뿜뿜 뿜뿜 어nae balkkeutkkaji ppumppum ppumppum eo / Just feel it 뿜뿜Just feel it ppumppum / 네 앞에서 난 뿜뿜ne apeseo nan ppumppum / 네게 줄게 뿜뿜 뿜뿜 어nege julge ppumppum ppumppum eo / 지금 보고 있는 게 꿈은 아닐 걸jigeum bogo inneun ge kkumeun anil geol / 땡땡이치고 날 만나게 될 걸ttaengttaeng-ichigo nal mannage doel geol / 매력을 야 뿜어뿜어뿜어뿜어maeryeogeul ya ppumeoppumeoppumeoppumeo
verse_2.literal: Right now, in my eyes, in my eyes, in my eyes / your shoulders, knees, feet / I feel like I can't breathe / whenever I just look at you
verse_2.context: 숨이 막히다 (for one's breath to be blocked/choked) is a common expression for being overwhelmed, here used almost literally comically alongside a body-part list (어깨 무릎 발, shoulders knees feet) that borrows the rhythm of a Korean children's song, adding a playful, silly edge to an otherwise breathless infatuation lyric.

chorus.lines: 보여줄게 pick up the phoneboyeojulge pick up the phone / Wow, wow 정신없이Wow, wow jeongsineopsi / 쿵 쿵 내 마음을 뿜 뿜 사정없이 또kung kung nae ma-eumeul ppum ppum sajeong-eopsi tto / Ooh 여기서 뭘 어떻게 더Ooh yeogiseo mwol eotteoke deo / 너 낮이나 밤이나 빛이나 미쳤나봐neo najina bamina bichina michyeonnabwa / 떨리지 막 떨려와tteolliji mak tteollyeowa / 이제 나만 생각 날 거야ije naman saenggak nal geoya / 밤에 잠도 잘 못 잘 거야bame jamdo jal mot jal geoya / 점점 더 fall in lovejeomjeom deo fall in love / My 눈눈눈눈눈눈 눈빛My nunnunnunnunnunnun nunbit / 쏟아지는ssodajineun / My 터터터터터터 터치My teoteoteoteoteoteo teochi / 하나뿐인hanappunin / 내 머리부터 뿜뿜nae meoributeo ppumppum
chorus.literal: Give it to you / my eyes eyes eyes eyes eyes eyes, my gaze pouring out / my touch touch touch touch touch touch, my one and only / my lo-lo-lo-lo-lo, my lover / from my head, bboom bboom / to the tips of my toes, bboom bboom bboom bboom
chorus.context: The stuttered repetition (눈눈눈눈눈눈, 터터터터터터) mimics a skipping heartbeat or racing pulse rather than literal stammering — it's a vocal effect standing in for the physical sensation of nervous excitement. 머리부터 발끝까지 (from head to the very tips of the toes) is a common Korean expression for something affecting your entire body, head to toe.

bridge.literal: What you're seeing right now probably isn't a dream / wake up, wake up / you'll end up skipping [class/work] to come meet me / take off, take off
bridge.context: 땡땡이치다 is a casual verb meaning to skip class, ditch work, play hooky — a specifically youthful, mischievous image of choosing her over responsibilities, matching the song's overall playful, slightly bratty confidence.

artist_context: MOMOLAND formed through the survival show Finding Momoland and had a relatively quiet start before BBoom BBoom's simple, highly imitable finger-heart-gun dance turned into a viral sensation across Korea and beyond in 2018, rapidly changing the group's trajectory — a clear example of how a single, extremely shareable hook can outperform more polished but less meme-friendly songs in K-pop.

grammar_highlights.usage: 'To alternate doing X and Y repeatedly.' 들었다 놨다 해 — 'picks it up and puts it down, over and over' — an idiom for inconsistent, back-and-forth behavior.
'Feels like ~, seems like ~.' 숨이 막힐 것 같아 — 'feels like I can't breathe' — describing a strong physical/emotional reaction as a perception.
'[You'll] end up ~ing.' 만나게 될 걸 — 'you'll end up meeting me' — predicting an inevitable outcome with playful confidence.
